fact_previews: Ivelin Demirov created the Interactive Python tutorials project.
The project aims to teach Python 3.0 programming through interactive methods such as drag and drop games, quizzes, and exercises.
The project received CA$ 21,926 from 1,009 backers on Kickstarter.
The funding period for the project was from March 1, 2015, to April 5, 2015.
The project had a funding goal of CA$ 1,500.

The Interactive 'Learn Python VISUALLY' App is a result of improvements made based on feedback from previous projects.
Demirov's previous books, 'Learn JavaScript Visually' and 'Learn Python Visually', demonstrated that the educational system is effective.
The project aims to help individuals who have struggled to learn the Python language.
Demirov expresses strong conviction that the project will benefit many who wish to learn programming basics.

fact_previews: The project features four tablet screens displaying different educational content related to Python programming.
The Concatenation Screen illustrates string concatenation using graphics and includes a list of string examples.
The Variables Screen depicts boxes with labels to explain variables and is accompanied by code snippets demonstrating how variables work.
The Operator Precedence Screen shows graphical elements to illustrate operator precedence and includes symbols for different operators.
The DOM Node Tree Screen displays a hierarchical structure diagram for the DOM tree and includes colored blocks representing elements and attributes.
